context.title: The Glory Fills the Temple
context.summary: The ark is brought into the temple, the cloud of God's glory fills it, and Solomon prays a long dedication prayer asking God to hear every prayer made toward this house.
context.background: The dedication comes in the seventh month, at the Feast of Tabernacles (v. 2). Solomon's prayer even pictures Israel carried away captive (vv. 46–50) — words that spoke directly to the exiles who first read Kings.

customs.note: Israelites far away turned toward Jerusalem to pray. Daniel does exactly this in Babylon (Daniel 6:10).
Most of the meat was eaten by the worshipers in a shared meal, so the vast number of animals fed a vast crowd.

watchFor: The great question: 'will God indeed dwell on the earth?' (v. 27).
Solomon prays even for the foreigner who comes to pray (vv. 41–43).

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Zion
places.summary: Sunny; height, one of the eminences on which Jerusalem was built. It was surrounded on all sides, except the north, by deep valleys, that of the Tyropoeon separating it from Moriah, which it surpasses in height by 105 feet.

places.name: most holy place
places.summary: One of the two portions into which the tabernacle was divided (Ex. 26:31; 37:17-25; Heb. 9:2). It was 20 cubits long and 10 in height and breadth.

places.name: Holy Place
places.summary: One of the two portions into which the tabernacle was divided (Ex. 26:31; 37:17-25; Heb. 9:2). It was 20 cubits long and 10 in height and breadth.

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Horeb
places.summary: Desert or mountain of the dried-up ground, a general name for the whole mountain range of which Sinai was one of the summits (Ex. 3:1; 17:6; 33:6; Ps. 106:19, etc.).

events.title: Reign of Solomon
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 2:12–11:42. People: Solomon. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 40 years.
